# Equipment and Personnel Standards
These are non-modifiable SOP's that cannot be changed unless approved by a member of Provost.
## Standard Issue Equipment - Personnel must use standard-issue equipment or equipment available from Rifleman vendors. Unless provided equipment from a department with permission from the head of that department. Such as aircrew armor requiring permission from a dropship pilot. - Alcohol must be stored in the Officers' Mess or an officer's office.
## Uniform Regulations Personnel must wear appropriate clothing during operations. SOP may not be changed to allow personnel to deploy without clothing or a uniform. - Intelligence officers, with the commander's permission, may exempt themselves from all uniform regulations in relation to wearing military clothing, boots, headwear and weaponry. - Deploying personnel must wear a uniform, boots, and chest protective armour at minimum. Suit webbings may replace chest armour. - Personnel required to wear armour at all times may remove it while on a friendly ship or installation, or after an operation for social events such as memorials. Service jackets and other clothing may be worn during this time. - Personnel must wear their uniform and assigned footwear or a standard-issue replacement. - Personnel must wear their rank pins. - Auxiliary staff and support crew should not wear armour unless the ship/base is on security alert or deploying to the AO. - MPs, Law Enforcement and flight crew may wear armour shipside as part of their duties. - Headwear must be standard issue or an acceptable replacement. Reasonable religious headwear is exempt. - Folding or shortening uniforms is permitted provided the uniform is not damaged. - Dress uniforms may be worn by shipside staff who are not deploying.
## Firearm Handling Regulations - Weapons must be holstered or slung when not in use, with the safety engaged. Personnel must be allowed to holster or sling their weapon on their first offence. - Weapons may only be fired at the firing range under normal circumstances, except for ceremonies or briefings. - Training equipment, including training grenades and ammunition, may only be used at firing ranges. - Weapons must be secured in designated areas such as racks or cabinets when unattended. - If no firing range is available, MPs may designate a temporary safe area for weapons discharge. - Personnel who are not deployed, Flight Crew, or Military Police may only carry a sidearm.
## Use of language Military personnel may be trained in multiple languages, but their use is restricted in certain situations. - The primary language is the language that all personnel are able to speak and understand. - Briefings, debriefings, memorials, and other formal events must use the unit's primary language. - Command orders, tactical planning, and other operation-related tasks must use the unit's primary language. - Radio traffic on military frequencies must use the unit's primary language. - Social gatherings, RNR, pre-briefing activities, and non-combat situations, personnel may use any understood language.
